https://hungarytoday.hu/budapest-approve.text: Budapest Approves Design for New Pedestrian Bridge to Óbuda Island Budapest’s chief architect has approved the design for the new pedestrian bridge on Óbuda Island. The 138-meter-long, 3.5-meter-wide bridge will be built entirely with private funding, developer Biggeorge Property told MTI on Tuesday. The company wrote that the “sleek, clean-lined,” accessible pedestrian bridge—equipped with an elevator and bike ramps—which will start from the central square of Waterfront City, a development they are building, will span the HÉV (Budapest’s suburban commuter rail system), the riverbank, and a branch of the Danube, creating a direct connection to Óbuda Island. Equipped with public lighting and decorative lighting, the bridge will be the island’s fourth bridge—after the Árpád Bridge, the K Bridge, and the H Bridge—but the first designed specifically for pedestrians. The concept for the pedestrian bridge was developed by Speciálterv. Based on the reports, the documentation—which has been coordinated with the relevant authorities and utility providers—could be submitted for approval within weeks. The developer emphasized: this public-purpose investment, costing billions, will be funded entirely from private sources, and—along with the residents of the Waterfront projects—it will provide thousands of residents from neighboring housing estates with access to the island’s parks within a few minutes’ walk. The announcement also noted that, as part of the Waterfront Park project, significant transportation improvements will be made in addition to the pedestrian bridge, and the 70-year-old utility network will also be upgraded. In addition, several hundred public parking spaces will be built or renovated in the area to meet the increased parking needs of the previously constructed residential buildings. The project will continue with the scheduled construction of the Promenade, and the street connecting Szentendrei Road and the Filatorigát HÉV station will also be completed; the developer is providing the land for this project free of charge. Waterfront Park will also feature 130 municipal rental apartments, which the Budapest Municipal Government will lease from the developer at a discounted rate, while the Óbuda Municipal Government will receive 1.2 billion forints (approximately €3.3 million) from the company for the development of social infrastructure and the construction of rental housing. https://www.dw.com/en/south-park-satiris.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5NTB0 The Chi Phi fraternity was barred from campus in 2024 Image: Heather Ainsworth/AP Photo/picture alliance Advertisement Toby Morton, who wrote several episodes of the animated comedy series South Park , launched a website seeking accountability in connection with an alleged 2024 sexual assault case involving seven fraternity members at Cornell University in the US . The site names seven men accused of sexually assaulting a 20-year-old woman who was allegedly unconscious after being given drugs and alcohol at a Cornell fraternity house, and collects personal data and photos of the members involved. "I've received messages reminding me I'm not a journalist, I'm 'just a satirist,'" Morton wrote in a September 27 Instagram post regarding the creation of his website TheCornell7.org. "This is true, but it makes me more dangerous," he added, saying he has "nobody to tell me I've gone too far." The case has recently drawn a surge in public attention after the accuser, identified as Jane Doe to protect her identity, filed a lawsuit in mid-September. Her complaint alleges that she was brutally sexually assaulted in 2024 by seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity while unconscious after being pressured to take ketamine, smoke marijuana and drink alcohol at the fraternity house on Cornell's campus in Ithaca, New York. The university, she said in the lawsuit, failed to protect her. Cornell conducted an internal investigation after the incident, but no one was charged. The reopening of the case has caused renewed attention on social media Image: Heather Ainsworth/AP Photo/picture alliance Since the lawsuit was filed on September 16, the case has generated widespread commentary on social media. Some have criticized Cornell and the district attorney's office, while others have questioned the allegations. Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten, who handled the original case, said his office has reopened it and plans to present evidence to a grand jury amid public questions about why no criminal charges were initially filed. Van Houten said in a statement that his office is considering bringing criminal charges related to the incident, though the allegations in the civil complaint are "dramatically different" from the woman's statement to police two years ago — in her statement to authorities, she did not allege she was drugged without her knowledge or that she did not consent to engage in sexual acts . Justice sought Cornell's Chi Phi chapter was barred from campus after the alleged incident in 2024. The woman who accused the men of sexual assault dropped out of Cornell University, according to her attorney. One of the most chilling allegations of the lawsuit is that a message was sent to a Chi Phi Snapchat group at about 1:42 a.m., inviting members to the room to abuse Doe, who was heavily under the influence of drugs and alcohol. The lawsuit alleges that more men then entered the room and that the assault continued for several hours until Doe lost consciousness. "There were so many people that could have prevented it and they didn't. I've never seen anything like it," an attorney for Jane Doe, Thomas Giuffra, told CBS. Giuffra pointed out that two of the seven accused fraternity members were expelled, while the others received lesser disciplinary measures. "Not one of these guys was arrested," Giuffra told the network. Actress Florence Pugh described the allegations as 'horrific' on social media Image: Cover Images/picture alliance Politicians and actors speak out Many people, from US politicians to Hollywood actors, have spoken out about the case in recent days. US Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, a New York Democrat, condemned what she described as a "culture of rape" protected by elite institutions. "When I read what happened at Cornell, those men posted in a group chat. That means it was normal to them. That means it was acceptable to them. This is a culture, and what we must do is understand that we cannot protect those spaces anymore," she said Sunday at a forum near Cornell's campus. British actress Florence Pugh described the allegations as "horrific" on social media and expressed her support for the student involved. Pugh, who is currently on a promotional tour for her upcoming Netflix series "East of Eden," wrote a lengthy statement on Instagram, saying that "Colleges/schools/universities repeatedly fail women around the world. You build men that get taught through time and time again that they can do extreme harm and that they won't be harmed in return." "Those who protect and impose light sentences on men who rape and destroy lives should be punished and closely scrutinized. Why are you protecting someone so fiercely?" she wrote. American actor Josh Gad, best known as the voice of Olaf in Disney's "Frozen" films, also commented on the Cornell case, criticizing what he described as insufficient disciplinary consequences for the students accused of sexual assault. In an Instagram post, Gad said sexual violence should not be treated as a mistake or addressed with limited disciplinary action by a university. He argued that the alleged conduct had "destroyed a life" and called for greater accountability. Edited by Joshua Lang. https://www.dailykos.com/stories/2026/10.text: Daily Kos Community Does Conservatism Always Lead to Fascism? by Thom Hartmann Community This content is not subject to review by Daily Kos staff prior to publication. Monday, October 26, 2026 at 8:21 AM PDT Recommend Story Share: Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Share on Bluesky (Opens in new window) Bluesky Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share using Native tools Share Copied to clipboard Save 54 Comments Add Daily Kos to Google Image by Gerd Altmann from Pixabay What happens when “conservatives” would rather destroy their democracy than surrender power? History shows us how that road leads straight to fascism, and Trump is taking America down it. When I was a kid I once asked my dad, who called himself an Eisenhower conservative, what “conservative” meant. He told me it wasn’t that different from liberalism but instead of favoring drastic or radical change in a society believed that such change should come gradually as the result of careful thought, debate, and incremental processes to minimize disruption to society. He quoted William F. Buckley saying, “A Conservative is a fellow who is standing athwart history yelling ‘Stop!’” My dad was a naive idealist who missed entirely the direction his “conservative” movement was heading. Conservatism has always, throughout history and in every country where it’s seized a strong foothold, been the precursor to the destruction of social cohesion ( look at “conservative” Macron’s France after 45 years of neoliberalism) and eventually violent fascism. Today’s American conservative movement began at our nation’s founding with the people who opposed our Revolutionary War, grew through the Old South as the plantation owners rose up and turned that region into a brutal oligarchy and declared war on our democracy, reappeared as Jim Crow and the 1940s’ America First movement, popped up again with Joe McCarthy and Roy Cohn, and is now full-blown with MAGA Trumpism and its billionaire backers. It thrives on fear and resentment while it embraces violence, authoritarianism, and great wealth, the basic hallmarks of fascism. Consider how when Abdul El-Sayed was challenged by a paid heckler he turned it into a thoughtful discussion, while in two of Trump’s rallies in the past week he’s encouraged his mob as they beat senseless people who dared challenge him or call for the release of the Epstein files. Or how Trump’s masked, armed ICE thugs have beaten, imprisoned, and even murdered American citizens with impunity while using terror tactics against dark-skinned non-citizens. In a 1957 editorial titled Why the South Must Prevail, Buckley laid out explicitly what the foundation of his then-reawakening conservative movement must be. “Again, let us speak frankly,” Buckley wrote : “The South does not want to deprive the Negro of a vote for the sake of depriving him of the vote. … In some parts of the South, the White community merely intends to prevail — that is all. It means to prevail on any issue on which there is corporate disagreement between Negro and White. The White community will take whatever measures are necessary to make certain that it has its way.” He asked, rhetorically, if white people in the South are “entitled” to “prevail” over nonwhites even in rural areas of the country or large cities with majority Black populations. “The sobering answer,” Buckley, the acknowledged godfather of today’s conservative movement, wrote, “is Yes — the White community is so entitled because, for the time being, it is the advanced race.” Arguably, following up in April of 2021 the National Review published an article headlined: Why Not Fewer Voters ? justifying Republican voter suppression. While conservativism in all its incarnations around the world has always embraced racism (look at what Modi is doing now in India , for example), it typically ends with iron-fisted fascism. And it’s here, now, in America. The Free Press (the original one, not Bari Weiss’ knock-off) just published a report titled Enemies of the State that analyses Trump’s National Security Presidential Memo 7 (NSPM-7). It orders the FBI, DHS, Treasury, and the IRS to aim every counterterrorism, tax, and surveillance tool they have at a target defined by nothing more than ideology, which the memo spells out as “anti-Americanism, anti-Christianity, and anti-capitalism.” Yes, the thought police are now here. Then-AG Bondi’s follow-up memos told federal prosecutors to go after protestors with the highest provable charges, build list of “Antifa-aligned entities,” open a tip line with cash rewards (Trump rolled this out last week under the rubric of “fraud”), and use terrorism as the excuse for the most severe punishments possible. Its first real test was a July 4th noisy demonstration outside the Prairieland ICE facility in Texas that did about $4,400 in property damage. One of the protestors, Benjamin Song, shot and wounded a police officer he claimed was aiming at an unarmed protestor, and he got 100 years in prison for his offense. Protestor Maricela Rueda got a 70 year sentence for being there and “conspiring” with Song, five others got 50 years in federal prison each, and Rueda’s husband — who wasn’t even at the protest — got a 30 year sentence for helping hide a box of zines. But the report’s real warning is what’s coming up next. The FBI now runs a multi-agency NSPM-7 Joint Mission Center drawing on staffers from roughly ten federal agencies looking for people whose opinions may be “anti-American.” The DOJ indicted the Southern Poverty Law Center in April, and in August arrested Heidi Beirich, the woman who spent two decades tracking the Klan and neo-Nazis for them. Treasury Secretary Bessent is reportedly drafting a plan to strip the tax exemptions of Open Society, SPLC and CAIR, and Homeland Security has investigated more than 150 nonprofits that register voters, claiming they’re nailing these groups to protect “election integrity.” As the authors, Shilpa Jindia and Nora Benavidez, put it plainly : “It treats speaking out, protesting and civic-engagement activities as ‘evidence of terrorism.’” — Richard Nixon was the first Republican in the modern era to openly dance with the fascists, welcoming southern white supremacist Democrats into the GOP after LBJ signed the Civil Rights and Voting Rights acts. His right-hand man John Ehrlichman laid it out plainly, describing the explicitly fascist intent behind Nixon’s so-called War On Drugs . — Reagan brought in the morbidly rich and Heritage and laid the foundation for the explosion of rightwing billionaires and their acquisition of our media and social media. He sent surplus military equipment to our police departments, turning them into something that more resembles an occupying army than a “serve and protect” group that Andy Griffiths would recognize. The reality is they’re not “conserving” anything. They’re instead echoing the thousands of years of modern history of kings and kingdoms where the ruler had absolute, life-or-death power over a nation’s subjects, and citizenship and freedom were both dependent on his whim. Hierarchy, patriarchy, and a few hundred billionaire families drive today’s Republican effort to defeat our Founders’ liberal democracy and replace it with a Russia-style authoritarian oligarchy and fascism. There’s no moral core to this so-called “patriotic” movement; just look at Ramaswamy’s despicable attacks on Dr. Amy Acton, Trump saying that “Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine; they haven’t been doing much” as the missiles murder civilians, and the GOP’s slanders questioning both Talarico’s sexuality and El-Sayed’s loyalty to America. It’s all about power and the money associated with it. Corruption is fine, so long as you don’t get caught. We now have more concentration camps in America than Hitler did at the end of his first year, and our wealth disparities are greater than any time in American history. For hundreds of thousands of years, as I document in The Hidden History of American Democracy , tribal people around the world mostly lived in egalitarian societies (there were exceptions, of course) where the “chief” was actually the servant of the tribe rather than its dictator. They were the archetype and model for the Founders of our republic and the Framers of our Constitution, a worldview and governing philosophy today being openly challenged by rightwing billionaires from the Trump family on down. The damage they’ve done to our republic and working class people — from Reagan’s Mandate for Leadership to Trump’s Project 2025 and alliances with Putin — is extraordinary. It’ll take a generation to undo, if America is to recover and become Lincoln’s “more perfect union.” But there’s considerable reason for hope; change is in the wind worldwide. The people of Hungary said “no” to fascism in April and turned out Putin’s puppet and Trump’s friend Orbán. The people of Serbia yesterday said “no” to fascism and turned out Putin’s toady and Trump’s friend Vučić. As did Brazilians when they rejected Trump/Putin friend Flavio Bolsonaro. Will we also say “no” to fascism and turn out the Republican lickspittles who revel in sucking up to Putin’s toady Trump? That effort begins with us, finally coming down to this week and early next, showing up to vote and continuing to speak out. Tag, we’re it! We continue to be supported by our readers, not billionaires or corporations. But we need to bring in more revenue. We are leaning on our community more than ever to help make ends meet.
